references.text: The Ammonites allied themselves with other enemies against Israel, as they also did here by crossing the Jordan to attack
A similar pattern where enemies crossed into Israel's land to attack and oppress them
The continuation of the conflict with the Ammonites that led to Jephthah being called to lead Israel
The background to the Ammonites' hostility and their claim on Israelite territory
The Ammonites came to fight against Israel, a recurring theme in Israel's history
Benjamin, Judah, and Ephraim are mentioned as tribes that were attacked, and these tribes had important territories
The prophecy that Israel would be pressed from all sides if they abandoned the Lord, as happened here
The Lord's hand was against Israel so that they were severely oppressed, a recurring theme in Judges
